decisions.reason: Using the L–V cadence as the wordmark-wide spacing reference does not change the second V height hierarchy; the separate hierarchy change in message 165 is already represented.
The optical-spacing standard does not change how the second V is constructed; message 165 already separately records the copied-and-scaled construction alternatives.
Adjusting spacing around the locked assets does not alter the preservation policy or unlock their geometry; the same-message update concerning the second V review is already represented.
The L–V cadence governs spacing between characters, not the E and L letterform geometry, proportions, terminals, or architectural vocabulary.
The spacing reference does not modify the approved Hero V geometry or its architectural role.
Balancing character-pair spacing does not change the requirement that the É accent be literally derived from the Hero V terminal.
The wordmark spacing standard does not alter the required horizontal peak alignment between the Hero V and É accent.
Optical spacing adjustments do not change the selected all-caps case treatment.
The spacing decision has no necessary effect on the deferred champagne-gold material treatment.
The L–V spacing reference does not change the requirement to deliver final production-ready artwork.
